_note: Every entry must have a _source_note documenting the primary source verified, the article text consulted, and the date verified. No TODO entries may ship. effective_from dates in ISO 8601.

frameworks.name: EU AI Act
frameworks._source_note: Verified against EUR-Lex OJ publication 2024/1689 and the amending Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026. Entry into force 1 August 2024. Phased application as amended: Art. 4 and Art. 5 from 2 Feb 2025; GPAI model obligations from 2 Aug 2025; Art. 50 transparency from 2 Aug 2026; new Art. 5(1)(ba)–(bb) prohibitions from 2 Dec 2026; Annex III high-risk obligations from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product-embedded) high-risk obligations from 2 Aug 2028. Verified October 2026.

framework_version.note: Digital Omnibus on AI in force 27 July 2026. Annex III high-risk obligations apply from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product-embedded) from 2 Aug 2028. Article 50 transparency applies from 2 Aug 2026.

frameworks.name: GDPR
frameworks._source_note: Verified against EUR-Lex OJ publication. In force since May 2018. Article 22 is the primary interaction point with AI automated-decision systems.

framework_version.note: In force since May 2018. Article 22 provisions unchanged by Digital Omnibus.

frameworks.name: NIST AI RMF
frameworks._source_note: Source URL updated to the official NIST framework page on 2026-10-07; mapping content not re-reviewed. NIST AI RMF 1.0 published January 2023. Non-regulatory — voluntary framework. Core functions: GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE.

framework_version.note: Non-regulatory — voluntary framework. AI 600-1 addresses generative AI risks. NIST has announced a revision of AI RMF 1.0; no successor version published as at October 2026.

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 42001
frameworks._source_note: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 published December 2023. International standard for AI management systems. Voluntary but increasingly referenced by regulators.

framework_version.note: First edition, December 2023. International standard for AI management systems.

frameworks.name: OWASP LLM Top 10
frameworks._source_note: OWASP GenAI Security Project, Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026 (LLM01:2026–LLM10:2026), published August 2026; ranking combines practitioner voting with an incident corpus. Verified against the project's final 2026 text, October 2026. Non-regulatory — security community best practice. Primary relevance: systems using LLMs.

framework_version.note: Non-regulatory — security community best practice. 2026 edition supersedes 2025: Excessive Agency rises to LLM03; System Prompt Leakage becomes Hidden Context Exposure (LLM08). Agentic systems: see also the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications.

frameworks.name: OWASP Agentic Top 10
frameworks._source_note: OWASP GenAI Security Project, Top 10 for Agentic Applications (branded 2026), released 9 December 2025. Extends rather than replaces the LLM Top 10. Non-regulatory. Verified October 2026.

framework_version.citation: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026
framework_version.note: Non-regulatory — security community best practice for autonomous and tool-using AI systems. Use alongside the LLM Top 10.

frameworks.name: AU Privacy Act
frameworks.long_name: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) including Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024
frameworks._source_note: Privacy Act 1988 as amended. The Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024 (Royal Assent 10 Dec 2024) inserts automated-decision-making transparency requirements (APP 1.7–1.9) commencing 10 December 2026. OAIC final guidance (updated APP 1 Guidelines and APP 1.7–1.9 fact sheet) released September 2026. Verified October 2026.

framework_version.citation: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) as amended by Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024
framework_version.note: ADM transparency obligations (APP 1.7–1.9) commence 10 Dec 2026. OAIC final guidance released September 2026.

frameworks.name: APRA CPS 230
frameworks.long_name: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 230 — Operational Risk Management
frameworks._source_note: CPS 230 effective 1 July 2025 for most APRA-regulated entities (ADIs, insurers, RSE licensees, private health). Requires impact tolerances, business continuity plans, and material service provider management. Verified against APRA published standard July 2023.

framework_version.note: Effective 1 July 2025 for most APRA-regulated entities.

frameworks.name: AU Guidance for AI Adoption
frameworks.long_name: Australian Government Guidance for AI Adoption (replaces the Voluntary AI Safety Standard)
frameworks._source_note: Published by the National AI Centre (Department of Industry, Science and Resources), October 2025, as the first update to the 2024 Voluntary AI Safety Standard. Condenses the 10 guardrails into 6 essential practices, in Foundations and Implementation practices editions. Voluntary — the government has not proceeded with mandatory guardrails. Verified October 2026.

framework_version.citation: Guidance for AI Adoption (National AI Centre, October 2025)
framework_version.note: Voluntary. Supersedes the Voluntary AI Safety Standard (2024); its 10 guardrails map to the 6 essential practices.

frameworks.name: UK Data Use and Access Act
frameworks._source_note: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, chapter 18, Royal Assent 19 June 2025. Replaces UK GDPR Article 22 with Articles 22A–22D (automated decision-making); commenced 5 February 2026 by SI 2026/82. Verified October 2026.

framework_version.note: Automated decision-making provisions (UK GDPR Arts 22A–22D) in force since 5 Feb 2026 (SI 2026/82).

frameworks.name: UK ICO AI Guidance
frameworks.long_name: ICO Guidance on AI and Data Protection
frameworks._source_note: ICO AI guidance portal. Updated periodically — last verified May 2026. Covers explaining AI decisions, fairness, accuracy, security. Non-binding guidance with regulatory expectation weight.

framework_version.citation: ICO Guidance on AI and Data Protection
framework_version.note: Non-binding guidance with regulatory expectation weight. Updated periodically — last verified May 2026.

mappings.title: High-risk classification — credit scoring of natural persons
mappings.summary: AI systems used for creditworthiness assessment or credit scoring of natural persons (excluding fraud detection in financial services) are high-risk. This triggers the full set of high-risk obligations in Articles 9–15 and 26.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Annex III, point 5(b): AI systems intended to be used to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons or establish their credit score, with the exception of AI systems used for the purpose of detecting financial fraud. (Corrected October 2026: earlier note quoted the 2021 Commission proposal wording.) Verified against EUR-Lex text May 2026. Application date moved from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026 (Art. 113(c)(i) as amended); 2 Aug 2028 where the system is high-risk via Annex I product legislation.

mappings.title: High-risk classification — employment and workers management
mappings.summary: AI systems used for recruitment, selection, promotion, task allocation, monitoring, or evaluation of persons in employment relationships are high-risk.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Annex III, point 4: employment, workers management and access to self-employment. Verified against EUR-Lex text May 2026. Application date moved from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026 (Art. 113(c)(i) as amended); 2 Aug 2028 where the system is high-risk via Annex I product legislation.

mappings.citation: Article 6(1) + Annex I — medical device safety components
mappings.title: High-risk classification — healthcare safety components
mappings.summary: AI systems that are medical devices, or safety components of medical devices, requiring third-party conformity assessment under the Medical Devices or In Vitro Diagnostic Regulations are high-risk under Article 6(1) and Annex I. Obligations apply from 2 August 2028 following the Digital Omnibus.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 6(1) and Annex I, Section A (Regulations (EU) 2017/745 and 2017/746). Corrected October 2026: previously cited as Annex III point 5(a), which covers eligibility for public assistance benefits, not medical devices. Application date 2 Aug 2028 per Art. 113(c)(ii) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026.

mappings.title: AI literacy obligation
mappings.summary: Providers and deployers of AI systems must take measures to support the development of AI literacy among their staff and others operating AI systems on their behalf, taking account of their knowledge, experience and the context of use. As amended by the Digital Omnibus, this does not require guaranteeing a specific level of literacy for any individual. Applies to all AI systems — not only high-risk.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 4, applicable from 2 February 2025 per Article 113. Wording amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026: obligation is now to 'support the development of' AI literacy rather than 'ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level'. Verified against EUR-Lex October 2026.

mappings.title: Risk management system for high-risk AI
mappings.summary: Providers must establish, implement, document, and maintain a risk management system covering the entire lifecycle of the high-risk AI system. The system must identify foreseeable risks, estimate and evaluate them, adopt appropriate measures, and provide for post-market monitoring.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 9. Applies to high-risk AI systems (Annex III). Verified against EUR-Lex text May 2026. Application date moved from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026 (Art. 113(c)(i) as amended); 2 Aug 2028 where the system is high-risk via Annex I product legislation.

mappings.title: Risk management system for high-risk AI
mappings.summary: Providers must establish, implement, document, and maintain a risk management system covering the entire lifecycle of the high-risk AI system. Covers identification of foreseeable risks, evaluation, mitigation, and residual risk acceptance, with ongoing post-market monitoring.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 9. High-risk system trigger: Annex III categories. Verified May 2026. Application date moved from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026 (Art. 113(c)(i) as amended); 2 Aug 2028 where the system is high-risk via Annex I product legislation.

mappings.title: Training, validation and testing data requirements
mappings.summary: Training, validation and testing datasets must meet quality criteria: relevance, representativeness, freedom from errors where possible, and appropriateness of statistical properties relevant to the persons on which the system is to be used.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 10. High-risk system requirement. Verified May 2026. Application date moved from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026 (Art. 113(c)(i) as amended); 2 Aug 2028 where the system is high-risk via Annex I product legislation.

mappings.citation: Article 13 — Transparency and provision of information to deployers
mappings.title: Instructions for use — transparency to deployers
mappings.summary: Providers must supply deployers with instructions for use covering: intended purpose, performance characteristics, foreseeable misuse, circumstances that may affect accuracy, human oversight requirements, and technical measures available to the deployer.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 13. Applies to all high-risk AI systems. For vendor-procured systems, the deployer must obtain and rely on these instructions. Verified May 2026. Application date moved from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026 (Art. 113(c)(i) as amended); 2 Aug 2028 where the system is high-risk via Annex I product legislation.

mappings.title: Human oversight measures
mappings.summary: High-risk AI systems must be designed and developed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during their use. Deployers must be able to intervene, halt, or override the system. Note: fully automated decisions with no human review create tension with this obligation.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 14. Requires designated natural persons with competence and authority to exercise oversight. Verified May 2026. Application date moved from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026 (Art. 113(c)(i) as amended); 2 Aug 2028 where the system is high-risk via Annex I product legislation.

mappings.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity requirements
mappings.summary: High-risk AI systems must be designed to achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity. Resilience to errors, faults, and inconsistencies (including adversarial inputs) must be considered.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 15. Verified May 2026. Application date moved from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026 (Art. 113(c)(i) as amended); 2 Aug 2028 where the system is high-risk via Annex I product legislation.

mappings.citation: Article 26 — Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
mappings.title: Deployer obligations
mappings.summary: Deployers must: use the system in accordance with instructions; assign human oversight to natural persons with appropriate competence; ensure input data is relevant and representative; inform affected workers; monitor operation; keep logs for at least six months.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 26. Applies where you are a deployer (not just provider) of a high-risk system. Verified May 2026. Application date moved from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026 (Art. 113(c)(i) as amended); 2 Aug 2028 where the system is high-risk via Annex I product legislation.

mappings.title: Fundamental rights impact assessment (FRIA)
mappings.summary: Before first use of an Annex III high-risk system, deployers that are bodies governed by public law or private entities providing public services, and any deployer of credit-scoring or life and health insurance risk-pricing systems (Annex III 5(b)–(c)), must conduct a fundamental rights impact assessment. Covers affected categories of persons, foreseeable harms, human oversight, and governance arrangements; may build on an existing GDPR DPIA.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 27. Applies to public-body deployers and private entities providing services to the public at scale. Financial services customer-facing systems are in scope. Notification to market surveillance authority required. Verified May 2026. Application date moved from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026 (Art. 113(c)(i) as amended); 2 Aug 2028 where the system is high-risk via Annex I product legislation. The Omnibus also lets deployers build the FRIA on an existing GDPR data protection impact assessment (Art. 27(4) as amended). Summary corrected October 2026: scope is set by Art. 27(1), not by the scale of personal data processing.

mappings.citation: Article 86 — Right to explanation of individual decision-making
mappings.title: Right to explanation for AI-assisted decisions
mappings.summary: Any person subject to a decision based on a high-risk AI system that produces legal or significant effects may request an explanation of the AI's role and the main elements of the decision. Deployers must provide meaningful explanations.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 86. Applies to natural persons subject to decisions by high-risk AI systems. Interacts with GDPR Article 22 right to explanation. Verified May 2026. Application date moved from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026 (Art. 113(c)(i) as amended); 2 Aug 2028 where the system is high-risk via Annex I product legislation.

mappings.title: Transparency for AI interactions and synthetic content
mappings.summary: Applies to all relevant AI systems, not only high-risk. Providers must design systems that interact with people so users are informed they are dealing with AI, and must mark synthetic audio, image, video and text output in a machine-readable, detectable way. Deployers of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation must inform the people exposed, and deployers must disclose deepfakes and AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 50, applicable from 2 August 2026 per Article 113 — not deferred by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026. Transitional period: providers of generative systems placed on the market before 2 Aug 2026 must comply with Art. 50(2) marking by 2 Dec 2026 (Art. 111(4) as amended). Commission Article 50 guidelines and Code of Practice on marking AI-generated content in preparation during 2026. Added October 2026.

mappings.title: Prohibition: non-consensual intimate imagery and child sexual abuse material
mappings.summary: Placing on the market or using AI systems that generate or manipulate realistic intimate imagery of an identifiable person without their explicit consent, or child sexual abuse material, is prohibited. Providers are caught where this is the intended purpose or a reasonably foreseeable, reproducible outcome without adequate safeguards — so image, video and audio generators need effective safeguards in place.
mappings._source_note: New prohibitions inserted into Article 5(1) points (ba) and (bb), with Art. 5(1a)–(1b), by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026. Apply from 2 December 2026 per Art. 113(a) as amended. Added October 2026.

mappings.title: General-purpose AI models — provider duties and downstream information rights
mappings.summary: Obligations under Articles 53–55 fall on providers of general-purpose AI models (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google), which must maintain technical documentation and make information available to downstream providers integrating the model. If you build on a GPAI model via API you are generally a downstream provider or deployer, not a GPAI provider: use the model provider's documentation and the GPAI Code of Practice signatory status in vendor due diligence. Fine-tuning that substantially modifies a model can make you a GPAI provider.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Articles 51–56, applicable from 2 August 2025 per Article 113(b); Commission enforcement powers from 2 August 2026. Corrected October 2026: previously dated 2 Aug 2026 and framed as a deployer obligation.

mappings.title: Right not to be subject to solely automated decisions
mappings.summary: Data subjects have the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects, unless based on explicit consent, contractual necessity, or authorised by Member State law. Where such decisions are made, individuals must have the right to human intervention, to express their point of view, and to contest the decision.
mappings._source_note: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 Article 22. In force since May 2018. Credit decisions are explicitly within scope ('legal or similarly significant effect'). Verified May 2026.

mappings.title: Privacy Act 1988 — automated decision-making notice requirements
mappings.summary: From 10 December 2026, privacy policies must explain where a computer program uses personal information to make, or to do something substantially and directly related to making, decisions that could significantly affect an individual's rights or interests. OAIC guidance confirms this reaches decision-support tools and embedded software, not only fully automated decisions, and applies to decisions made after commencement even if the data was collected earlier.
mappings._source_note: Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024, Schedule 1, inserting APP 1.7–1.9; commences 10 December 2026. OAIC final guidance (APP 1 Guidelines update and APP 1.7–1.9 fact sheet) released September 2026. Scope widened in October 2026 review to include decision-support configurations. Verified October 2026.

mappings.title: Privacy Act — Australian Privacy Principles
mappings.summary: Any AI system processing personal information of Australian individuals must comply with the APPs. Relevant principles: APP 1 (privacy policy), APP 3 (collection), APP 6 (use and disclosure), APP 11 (security). The 2024 amendments strengthen notification and consent requirements.
mappings._source_note: Privacy Act 1988 Australian Privacy Principles. Applies to organisations with >$3M annual turnover (and some others). Verified against OAIC guidance May 2026.

mappings.title: APRA CPS 230 — operational risk and AI systems
mappings.summary: APRA-regulated entities (ADIs, insurers, RSE licensees) must manage operational risks including those from AI systems used in critical operations. Requires impact tolerances, business continuity planning, and material service provider arrangements. Credit decisioning would typically qualify as a critical operation.
mappings._source_note: APRA CPS 230 effective 1 July 2025. Applies to APRA-regulated entities. AI systems used in critical operations must be included in operational risk management frameworks. Verified against APRA published standard and information papers May 2026.

mappings.title: AU Guidance for AI Adoption — 6 essential practices
mappings.summary: The Australian Government's Guidance for AI Adoption (October 2025) replaces the Voluntary AI Safety Standard. Its six essential practices are: decide who is accountable; understand impacts and plan accordingly; measure and manage risks; share essential information; test and monitor; maintain human control. Voluntary, but the reference point for responsible AI expectations in Australia.
mappings._source_note: Guidance for AI Adoption, National AI Centre, October 2025 — Foundations and Implementation practices editions. First update to the Voluntary AI Safety Standard (September 2024); the 10 guardrails are consolidated into 6 practices. Voluntary. Verified October 2026.

mappings.title: NIST AI RMF — GOVERN: policies, accountability, culture
mappings.summary: Organisational policies, accountability structures, roles and responsibilities, and culture for trustworthy AI are established. Includes AI risk tolerance definition, and clear ownership of AI governance. Recommended baseline for any AI governance programme.
mappings._source_note: Source URL updated to the official NIST framework page on 2026-10-07; mapping content not re-reviewed. NIST AI RMF 1.0, GOVERN function. Published January 2023. Cross-referenced by AU Voluntary AI Safety Standard and ISO 42001. Verified May 2026.

mappings.title: ISO/IEC 42001 — AI Management System
mappings.summary: ISO/IEC 42001 specifies requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an AI management system. Particularly relevant for organisations seeking third-party certification of their AI governance practices.
mappings._source_note: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 published 18 December 2023. Voluntary international standard. Increasingly referenced in enterprise procurement requirements and regulatory guidance. Verified May 2026.

mappings.title: OWASP LLM Top 10 — security risks for LLM applications
mappings.summary: The OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2026) covers: prompt injection (LLM01), sensitive information disclosure (LLM02), excessive agency (LLM03), supply chain (LLM04), data and model poisoning (LLM05), unbounded consumption (LLM06), misinformation (LLM07), hidden context exposure (LLM08), vector and embedding weaknesses (LLM09) and improper output handling (LLM10).
mappings._source_note: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026, final text in the GenAI Security Project repository, checked October 2026. Replaces the 2025 edition. Voluntary security community standard. Relevant for any system using LLMs.

mappings.title: OWASP Agentic Top 10 — security risks for autonomous AI agents
mappings.summary: Security risks specific to agents that plan, use tools and act with delegated permissions — including goal hijacking, tool misuse, identity and privilege abuse, memory poisoning, and cascading failures across multi-agent systems. Use alongside the LLM Top 10, which agentic systems also inherit.
mappings._source_note: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026, released 9 December 2025 by the OWASP GenAI Security Project. Voluntary security community guidance. Added October 2026.

mappings.citation: UK GDPR Articles 22A–22D (Data (Use and Access) Act 2025)
mappings.title: UK automated decision-making — safeguards regime (Arts 22A–22D)
mappings.summary: Since 5 February 2026, UK GDPR permits solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on most personal data, provided safeguards are in place: tell individuals about the decision, let them make representations, obtain human intervention, and contest the decision. Stricter limits remain where special category data is used.
mappings._source_note: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 replaced UK GDPR Article 22 with Articles 22A–22D; commenced 5 February 2026 by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 (Commencement No. 6 and Transitional and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/82). Corrected October 2026: previously described the former Article 22 restriction and dated from Royal Assent.

mappings.citation: ICO AI Guidance — fairness and bias
mappings.title: ICO AI Guidance — fairness, accuracy, and bias management
mappings.summary: The ICO expects organisations using AI to process personal data to actively address fairness risks. This includes bias testing, documentation of training data characteristics, and ongoing monitoring for discriminatory outcomes.
mappings._source_note: ICO AI Guidance portal — fairness section. Updated periodically. Reflects ICO regulatory expectations under UK GDPR. Verified May 2026.
